The exams

Combined or Triple?

Combined Science is worth two GCSEs and covers a core of Biology, Chemistry and Physics. Triple Science (separate Biology, Chemistry and Physics) is three GCSEs with more content. Combined is typically examined in six papers; Triple in two per science. Your school decides which one a student sits, and I teach both.

Exam technique

Where marks are usually lost

  • Rearranging equations and keeping track of units in Physics calculations
  • Extended-response questions with no clear structure
  • Required practicals: method, variables and evaluating results
  • Imprecise use of key terms, such as “energy” versus “force”

FAQ

GCSE Combined & Triple Science: common questions

Combined or Triple Science?

Your school enters each student for one or the other. Combined Science is two GCSEs; Triple Science is three separate GCSEs. Sessions follow whichever your child is sitting.

Are the required practicals part of the exam?

Yes. Questions on the required practicals appear in the written papers, so method, variables and evaluation are all worth practising.

Which exam boards do you teach?

AQA, Edexcel and OCR, among others. Sessions are tailored to the board your school sits.
